__comment: Generated SMILES overrides keyed by substance slug. Produced by the gap-fill batches (PubChem/Wikipedia) for substances missing inline identification.smiles. Every entry RDKit-validated. `represents` names the active molecule when the substance is a plant, preparation, or brand name. Depictions render from Postgres moleculeOverrides (seed with npm run molecules:seed).

25-dma.note: Name not found directly; '25-DMA' = 2,5-dimethoxyamphetamine per the 2,5-dimethoxy ('25') naming convention. PubChem CID 62787.

25t-4-nbome.note: PubChem name lookup failed; identified as 25T4-NBOMe (NBOMe analogue of 2C-T-4, 4-isopropylthio). SMILES confirmed against PubChem CID 125181243.

3-meo-pcpy.note: Resolved via IUPAC name 1-[1-(3-methoxyphenyl)cyclohexyl]pyrrolidine. PubChem CID 137332196.

5-meo-mt.note: 5-methoxy-N-methyltryptamine (5-MeO-NMT); name 5-MeO-MT 404'd, resolved via synonym, PubChem CID 16184.

5-meo-nipt.note: 5-methoxy-N-isopropyl-N-methyltryptamine; resolved via full IUPAC-style synonym, PubChem CID 2763156. (Bare 'NiPT' name returns a wrong N-isopropyl-only structure.)

5-methylethylone.note: Ethylone (bk-MDEA) bearing a 5-methyl on the methylenedioxyphenyl ring; PubChem CID 112500536.

5-ppdi.note: Indane analog of alpha-PBP (2-pyrrolidin-1-yl-butanoyl-indane); PubChem CID 132989234.

6-mddm.note: dose.wiki article confirms 6-MDDM is the semisynthetic morphinan opioid 6-methylenedihydrodesoxymorphine (not an MDMA-class compound); PubChem CID 5492874.

a-pihp.note: alpha-pyrrolidinoisohexanophenone; resolved via synonym alpha-PiHP, PubChem CID 59809191.

alcohol.note: Active psychoactive constituent is ethanol; PubChem CID 702.

alpha-gpc.note: L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (choline alfoscerate), zwitterionic form; resolved via synonym, PubChem CID 657272.

amfonelic-acid.note: Dopaminergic stimulant naphthyridine carboxylic acid; PubChem CID 2137.

aminotadalafil.note: N-amino analog of tadalafil (PDE5 inhibitor); PubChem CID 10178467.

ashwagandha.note: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a plant; principal/marker active withanolide is withaferin A; PubChem CID 265237. (The herb's effects are attributed to a mix of withanolides; withaferin A chosen as the representative molecule per task guidance.)

bod.note: BOD = 4-methyl-2,5,beta-trimethoxyphenethylamine (beta-methoxy-2C-D), PiHKAL entry #14 confirmed via dose.wiki source; PubChem CID 44719486. (Note: bundled WIKIPEDIA source file is mislabeled with DOB content; ISOMERDESIGN/PiHKAL source is authoritative.)

cathinone.note: PubChem returns (S)-cathinone (natural enantiomer); racemic cathinone also exists.

changa.note: Changa is a smokable blend of DMT-containing extract and MAOI-containing herbs; principal psychoactive molecule is N,N-DMT.

chloral-betaine.note: Chloral betaine is a 1:1 complex of chloral hydrate and betaine; recorded as the two-component salt/adduct.

crl-40-940.note: CRL-40,940 = flmodafinil = bisfluoromodafinil = lauflumide; bis(p-fluoro) amide analog of modafinil (PubChem CID 13271852).

crl-40-941.note: CRL-40,941 = fladrafinil = fluorafinil; bis(p-fluoro) N-hydroxyacetamide prodrug of flmodafinil (PubChem CID 13316557). Verified against Wikipedia to distinguish from CRL-40,940.

cyclo-methiodrone.note: Novel research chemical (TCAT); IUPAC name piperidin-2-yl(thiophen-2-yl)methanone per TripSit. SMILES from PubChem CID 24261075 matching that IUPAC name. Limited literature.

datura.note: Datura is a botanical genus (e.g. jimsonweed) containing tropane alkaloids; principal psychoactive molecule represented here is scopolamine (also rich in atropine/hyoscyamine).

doip.note: DOiP = 2,5-dimethoxy-4-isopropylamphetamine, PubChem CID 44265275. Confirmed as DOx psychedelic amphetamine from source quotes; the name 'DOIP' alone in PubChem returns an unrelated phthalate plasticizer, which was rejected.

don.note: DON = 2,5-dimethoxy-4-nitroamphetamine, PubChem CID 105432. Confirmed as rare DOx psychedelic amphetamine from source quotes.

et.note: Article is αET (alpha-ethyltryptamine, marketed as Monase), PubChem CID 8367. Identity confirmed from source quotes referencing Upjohn 'Monase' and agranulocytosis.

ethaqualone.note: PubChem CID 23914 (etaqualone; 3-(2-ethylphenyl)-2-methylquinazolin-4-one, ethyl analogue of methaqualone).

f-phenibut.note: F-Phenibut = 4-fluorophenibut (4-amino-3-(4-fluorophenyl)butanoic acid), PubChem CID 103611. Same molecule as the 'Fluorophenibut' entry.

fasoracetam.note: PubChem CID 198695 (stereochemistry from PubChem isomeric SMILES).

fluorophenibut.note: Fluorophenibut = 4-fluorophenibut, PubChem CID 103611. Same molecule as the 'F-Phenibut' entry.

glaucine.note: PubChem CID 16754 (S-glaucine; stereochemistry from PubChem isomeric SMILES).

h-2c-b.note: Article is βH-2C-B = β-hydroxy-2C-B (2-amino-1-(4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenyl)ethanol), PubChem CID 11370394. Identity confirmed from source pharmacology quote describing 'β-Hydroxy-2C-B'.

hdep-28.note: PubChem CID 91844468 (ethyl ester naphthyl analogue of phenidate).

huperzine-a.note: Huperzine A, acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; stereochemistry-bearing SMILES, PubChem CID 854026.

ibuprofen.note: Ibuprofen (racemic; PubChem returns no stereocenter for the marketed mixture), CID 3672.

indapex.note: Indapex is a trade/alias name for 5-MeO-TMT (5-methoxy-2,N,N-trimethyltryptamine), a Shulgin tryptamine; PubChem CID 49756.

isophenmetrazine.note: Isophenmetrazine (5-methyl-3-phenylmorpholine regioisomer of phenmetrazine); PubChem CID 12945120.

isopropylphenidate.note: Isopropylphenidate (IPPH/IPH), isopropyl ester analogue of methylphenidate; PubChem CID 68314762.

kanna.note: Kanna (Sceletium tortuosum) is a plant; principal active alkaloid is mesembrine; PubChem CID 394162.

lae-32.note: LAE-32 is lysergic acid ethylamide (ergine ethyl analogue); stereochemistry-bearing form, PubChem CID 12304966.

lagochilus-inebrians.note: Lagochilus inebrians (Turkestan mint) is a plant; its characteristic diterpene constituent is lagochiline; PubChem CID 7061097.

librium.note: Librium is a brand name for chlordiazepoxide (benzodiazepine); PubChem CID 2712. [fixed: 4-oxide was mis-encoded as N-OH]

marinol.note: Marinol is a brand name for dronabinol, the synthetic delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol; PubChem CID 16078.

mdpa.note: MDPA = 3,4-methylenedioxy-N-propylamphetamine (the psychoactive Shulgin compound), PubChem CID 559375. The bare 'MDPA' PubChem name maps to an unrelated acetamide, so resolved via the full chemical name.

mebroqualone.note: Mebroqualone (2'-bromo methaqualone analogue, quinazolinone); PubChem CID 364842.

mephenaqualone.note: Mephenaqualone (8-methoxy-3-(2-methylphenyl)-2-phenylquinazolin-4(3H)-one, methaqualone analogue). Not in PubChem; SMILES from Wikipedia infobox, formula C22H18N2O2 (342.4) confirmed via RDKit.

methoxyketamine.note: Resolves to 2-methoxyketamine (2-MeO-ketamine), the commonly referenced isomer.

methoxypiperamide.note: Also known as MeOP / MEXP; PubChem CID 805654 lists 'Methoxypiperamide' as the primary name.

n-methylbisfluoromodafinil.note: Not found directly in PubChem under this name; SMILES is the N-methyl-4,4-difluoro modafinil structure (CAS 1613222-54-0) from PsychonautWiki/vendor reference standards.

neb.note: NEB is the common abbreviation for N-ethylbuphedrone (CID 20326296).

opium.note: Opium is a plant preparation (Papaver somniferum latex); SMILES is its principal psychoactive alkaloid, morphine (CID 5288826).

pargy-lad.note: N-propargyl lysergic acid diethylamide analog (PARGY-LAD), PubChem CID 139030999.

pbp.note: Source describes it as the homologue between alpha-PPP and alpha-PVP; this is alpha-PBP, PubChem CID 23199082.

pfbt.note: PFBT = 3-(p-fluorobenzoyloxy)tropane, a tropane local anaesthetic ~30% potency of cocaine (matches source). PubChem CID 5147770. Note: a literal PubChem name lookup of 'pFBT' wrongly returns pentafluorothiophenol, which was rejected.

phenetrazine.note: Ethyl homolog of phenmetrazine (3-ethyl-2-phenylmorpholine), PubChem CID 43350824.

pipt.note: PiPT is N-isopropyl-N-propyltryptamine, a psychedelic tryptamine (matches source effects). PubChem CID 57464898.

prl-8-53.note: Free base of PRL-8-53, PubChem CID 39989 (the HCl salt is CID 70700868); salt counterion removed.

pseudoephrine.note: Title 'Pseudoephrine' is a misspelling of pseudoephedrine, PubChem CID 7028.

pst.note: PST = poppy seed/straw tea, a preparation whose principal active opium alkaloid is morphine. PubChem CID 5288826.

pv-8.note: PV-8 is the higher homologue of alpha-PHP (matches source), i.e. alpha-pyrrolidinoheptaphenone. PubChem CID 69245534.

pvt.note: alpha-PVT, the thiophene analog of alpha-PVP (matches source). PubChem CID 71721462.

ronlax.note: Ronlax is a Mexican brand name for ethyl loflazepate, a long-half-life benzodiazepine metabolizing into descarboxyloflazepate (matches source). PubChem CID 3299.

salvia.note: Salvia divinorum; principal psychoactive constituent is salvinorin A (PubChem CID 128563).

sinicuichi.note: Sinicuichi = Heimia salicifolia; principal alkaloid commonly cited as cryogenine/vertine (PubChem CID 5315204).

sonata.note: Sonata is the brand name for zaleplon (PubChem CID 5719).

tobacco.note: Tobacco (Nicotiana); principal psychoactive constituent is nicotine (PubChem CID 89594).

yerba-mate.note: Yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis); principal psychoactive constituent is caffeine (PubChem CID 2519).
